clue.text: Chinese problem may be capable of understanding…

indicators.note: may be suggests the fourteen letters of the first two words could be something else once rearranged

explanation.surface: A tricky Chinese puzzle might turn out to be graspable after all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'problem' looks like the subject of the sentence but is anagram fodder along with 'Chinese'; 'may be' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Older usage lets the word mean intelligent or able to grasp ideas, as well as easily grasped.

parts.note: posting a letter is sending it, and chain armour is also called mail, so a letter in chain links suggests the same word twice

explanation.definitionFit: Posting items is sending them, and the word also suggests armour of linked metal rings.

clue.text: Ready to drop in Capri, perhaps

indicators.note: in shows the letters sit inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: Fruit on an Italian island is about to fall.
explanation.definitionFit: Fully mature fruit is ready to fall from the tree.

clue.text: The man's frenzy is of Spanish origin

parts.note: his means belonging to the man
panic is a frantic state of alarm

explanation.surface: A fellow's wild agitation comes from his Spanish roots.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes people or culture descended from Spain or Spanish-speaking lands.

indicators.note: behind says the letter for left is placed after the heroine

parts.note: Norma is the title heroine of Bellini's opera

explanation.surface: An ordinary opera heroine has been abandoned.
explanation.walkthrough: Vincenzo Bellini's opera Norma is named after its druid priestess heroine.
explanation.definitionFit: Something usual or typical conforms to the expected standard.

parts.note: barred reads as excluded, but literally means behind bars in a jail

explanation.definitionFit: Being locked in jail literally puts someone behind bars, away from society.

indicators.note: flexible suggests the letters can bend into another arrangement

parts.note: the name Emil with its possessive S gives five letters of fodder

explanation.surface: A man called Emil is remarkably supple.
explanation.definitionFit: Lithe and supple people bend easily, which is what being flexible means.

parts.note: a stick literally stuck in mud cannot move on, just as someone making no progress stays put

explanation.definitionFit: Making no progress at all means being stuck in place, like a stick lodged in mud.

clue.text: … like Pluto's problem, but he gets rid of it

parts.note: Dis is the Roman name for Pluto, god of the underworld
a poser is a puzzling problem

explanation.surface: Continuing the first clue: the underworld god's puzzle is one he simply throws away.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links back to 1-across's 'problem'; here Pluto's problem is read as Dis's poser.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who disposes of a thing is one who throws it away.

clue.text: It's spread from bygone days, note

parts.note: the past is the time of days gone by
E is a note of the musical scale

explanation.surface: Something smeared on bread is said to come from olden times plus a musical note.
explanation.definitionFit: Fish or meat paste is a smooth savoury spread for sandwiches.

clue.text: Amen to that, one may say

definitions.text: Amen to that, one may say

parts.words: Amen to that, one may say
parts.note: amen closes a prayer, so it is the final utterance, and the phrase also means a decisive final remark

explanation.definitionFit: Amen is the concluding utterance of a prayer, and the phrase means a final, decisive statement.

explanation.surface: Say hello to someone while caught in heavy rain.
explanation.definitionFit: To greet someone is to call out a welcome to them; a downpour of ice pellets falls as frozen precipitation.

indicators.note: change tells us to rearrange the letters of the three words that follow

explanation.surface: Rewriting a stage show turns out to be upsetting.
explanation.definitionFit: Something disastrous causes great distress, which is the sense of distressing here.

clue.text: An Amazon, perhaps, could resist his advances

definitions.text: An Amazon, perhaps, could resist his advances

parts.words: An Amazon, perhaps, could resist his advances
parts.note: a womaniser makes advances on women; read literally, his name suggests a killer of ladies, whom a warrior woman could fight off

explanation.definitionFit: A seducer of women is called this, as if he slays their hearts.

parts.note: fellers sounds like casual 'fellows' but means men who fell trees, and this is the wooden hut where lumberjacks sleep

explanation.definitionFit: Lumberjacks traditionally live in a hut built from felled tree trunks.

explanation.surface: An item of clothing worn for a folk dance.
explanation.definitionFit: It is both a short open jacket and a lively Spanish dance in triple time.

explanation.surface: A Mozart opera seems to be for ladies only.
explanation.walkthrough: Mozart's opera is known in English as The Abduction from the Seraglio.
explanation.definitionFit: Mozart's opera takes its name from the harem it is set in, and a harem is the secluded women's quarters.

clue.text: Soldiers who mutinied when the fat was in the fire, as it were

definitions.text: Soldiers who mutinied when the fat was in the fire, as it were

parts.words: Soldiers who mutinied when the fat was in the fire, as it were
parts.note: the idiom for trouble breaking out is taken literally: the 1857 Indian Mutiny was sparked by cartridges said to be greased with animal fat

explanation.walkthrough: These were Indian soldiers in British service; the rumour of cow and pig fat on rifle cartridges set off the 1857 rising.
explanation.definitionFit: Indian infantrymen serving the British East India Company started the 1857 rebellion.

parts.note: charge ahead suggests rushing forward, but is read as a charge levied a head, per person

explanation.walkthrough: Poll is an old word for head; the UK's per-person community charge of 1990 was widely called this.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a fixed levy on every adult, a charge per head.

clue.text: Intensely excited always when fish abound

indicators.note: abound is split as a-bound, bound around, so the fish wraps around the other piece

parts.note: ever means always, as in for ever

explanation.surface: An angler grows wildly worked up whenever the fish are plentiful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abound' looks like 'be plentiful' but is read as 'a-bound', meaning surrounding.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in a fever of anticipation means being wildly agitated.

clue.text: There's no escape in this situation

definitions.text: There's no escape in this situation

parts.words: There's no escape in this situation
parts.note: describes a deadlock or dead end where no way out exists

explanation.definitionFit: A deadlock is a position from which no progress or way out is possible.

indicators.note: topless means the first letter is removed from the word for being rueful

parts.note: regrets means is rueful about something

explanation.surface: Someone feels sorry about birds wearing no tops.
explanation.definitionFit: These are white herons with fine breeding plumes.

clue.text: Make lawman sigh for a place of pilgrimage

indicators.note: Make tells us to form something new from the letters of lawman and sigh

explanation.surface: A policeman is made to groan when sent to a holy site.
explanation.walkthrough: WALSINGHAM is a village in Norfolk, England, with a famous shrine to the Virgin Mary.
explanation.definitionFit: This Norfolk village has drawn pilgrims to its Marian shrine since medieval times.

indicators.note: back tells us the word for hits is read from right to left

parts.note: raps are sharp blows or knocks

explanation.surface: Someone lands return blows during a scrap.
explanation.definitionFit: To box lightly or argue is to engage in a mock fight.

parts.note: the Senior Service is the Royal Navy, abbreviated RN

explanation.surface: A naval officer is also an English composer.
explanation.walkthrough: The Royal Navy is called the Senior Service as Britain's oldest armed service; Thomas Arne wrote Rule, Britannia!
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Arne was the eighteenth-century English composer of Rule, Britannia!

clue.text: Beast allowed to return at burlington House

parts.note: Burlington House in London is home of the Royal Academy, abbreviated RA

indicators.note: to return asks for the word meaning allowed to be written backwards

parts.note: let means allowed or permitted

explanation.surface: An animal is permitted back at a London gallery.
explanation.walkthrough: The Royal Academy of Arts occupies Burlington House on Piccadilly in London.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the honey badger, a fierce African and Asian animal.

indicators.note: distributing suggests the letters of the generous gift are spread out in a new order

explanation.surface: A seaweed is handing out generous gifts.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a grass-like flowering plant that grows underwater along sea coasts.

explanation.surface: Travel in person quickly, or just speak up.
explanation.walkthrough: The first reading treats the phrase as 'travel yourself by fast delivery'.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally, to send yourself by speedy post; idiomatically, to put your thoughts into words, which is what saying means.
